messages.subject: Creating an error message
parts:
Hola R-ists. I'm having trouble trying to create an error message for
when a file doesn't have the search word I'm looking for. I want the
element number where the word first occurs so I can pull it and the
following element out:

element.num<-grep("word", file, perl=T, value=F)
element.num<-element.num[1]

When the word doesn't occur in a certain file, I get the result of
"integer (0)" for the first line of code and a result of "NA" for the
second line of code. So, I tried the following code to create an error
message, but to no avail:

if (element.num==NA)
stop("No word here")

I even tried the following, but still nothing:

if (element.num==integer (0))
if (element.num=="NA")
If (element.num=="integer (0)")

If it helps, the error message that R gives me when I run this code
is:

Error in if (element.num == NA) stop("No word here") :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I've found the ifelse() function, but I can't get it to work correctly
either.

The end goal is to either let the script continue until the end if the
word is found in the file, or stop the script and print the error
message if the word isn't found.

Any ideas? Thanks. Earl Brown
